full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal in short are: That the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as petitioners, filed above mentioned writ petition challenging proceeding of LA Case No. 13 of 2007 along with notice dated 7-10-2006 served under section 6 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 issued by the Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka, purporting to acquire the land of the writ petitioners at South Duttapara Mouza and South Ramchandrapur Mouza within Police Station-Savar, District-Dhaka for "Palli Bidduyut Samity". 

 3. It is stated that the present respondent No. 1 by three registered kabalas purchased 43.75 decimals of land from two plots being Plot Nos. 51 and 49 of Dakkhin Duttapara mouza under Savar Police Station and present respondent No. 2 also purchased 29 decimals of land from the said two plots by two registered kabalas. On the other hand, Dr Akhlaqur Rahman (since dead), husband of present respondent No. 1, purchased 84.50 decimals of land from plot No. 69 South Ramchandrapur Mouza and from Plots Nos. 51 and 49 of South Duttapara Mouza by five registered kabalas, which he ultimately transferred to his wife, the present respondent No. 1, by swearing affidavit before the Notary Public on 16-4-1992. Again Halida Rahman, daughter of respondent No. 1 purchased 14.50 decimals of land from the aforesaid Plot Nos. 51 and 49 by registered kabala and Ashfaq Tapan Rahman, son of the respondent No. 1 also purchased 43.75 decimals of land from the same plot Nos. 51 and 49 by three registered kabala deeds. Subsequently, Ashfaque and Halida Rahman executed two power-of-attorney deeds empowering respondent No. 1 for maintaining possession of their purchased lands and also for taking all necessary steps in respect of the same. Pursuant to such purchase and transfer the present respondents became owners of the aforesaid land and accordingly, got their names mutated and paid rents for the said lands to the government. While they were in possession of the above noted lands, the writ respondents initiated LA Case No. 13 of 2006-2007 to acquire the said land of the present respondents along with other lands for the purpose of setting up high voltage Power Sub-station for "Palli Budduyut Samity" at Savar without serving any notice as required under the provisions of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance of 1982) upon them. On 29-10-2007 the respondent No. 1 having received a telephone call came to learn that the aforesaid land has been acquired. On the same day, she also received three notices apparently under section 6 of the aforesaid Ordinance of 1982, signed on 8-10-2007, whereby the recipients of the said notices were directed to appear before the writ-respondent No. 2 on 25-10-2007. When she enquired in the office of the said respondent she was informed that 2.02 acres of plot Nos. 49, 51 and 69 belonging to them have been acquired. Upon visiting the said plots she found that the walls of the plots have been demolished and about 100 standing trees have been cut down. Hence the present respondents filed above noted writ petition claiming that the acquisition is illegal which has been vitiated for not specifying the lands sought to be acquired and that the said lands have not been acquired for public interest or for any public purpose and that no deed of agreement was executed between the requiring body and the Government, as required under section 15 of the said Ordinance of 1982 before acquiring the said lands and also for not serving any notice upon them and thereby obtained Rule Nisi and stay of the proceeding of LA Case No. 13 of 2007 along with operation of the notice served under section 6 of the said Ordinance, 1982. 

 4. In the said Rule Palli Biddyut Samity and Power Grid Company, Bangladesh Ltd. were added as respondents No. 7 and 8 respectively but only the writ respondent No. 8, Power Grid Company Ltd., (the present appellant), contested the Rule Nisi by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that the "Power Grid Company Ltd." (PGCL) and "Palli Bidduyut Samity" (REB) are the same authority who pursuant to Government decision and direction were entrusted with installing a high Volt Power Sub-Station around Savar area to meet the increasing demand of power because of rapid industrialisation, specially caused due to re-location of Tannery Industry at Savar. Thus the High Powered Committee of the Government and experts from REB and PGCL in consultation with each other and after thorough physical inspection/ investigation and feasibility tests decided to set up a 132/133 KV Power Sub-Station at the land belonging to the respondents and others. Accordingly the requiring body (PGCL and REB) entered into an agreement with the Government as per requirement of section 15 of the Ordinance, 1982 for acquisition of the said land which is done in public interest and for public purpose. Hence LA Case No. 13/2006-07 was initiated by issuing and serving notices under section 3 of the Ordinance 1982 upon the owners of the lands as well as on and near the lands proposed to be acquired. The present respondents (writ petitioners) pursuant to the said notice filed objection on 6-8-2007 and requested the Deputy Commissioner not to acquire her/their lands. Thereafter on 24-7-2007 subsequent notices were issued and served upon the present respondents fixing 5-8-2007 for hearing at the Deputy Commissioner's office on the objection, if any, raised; Then the matter was referred to the Divisional Commissioner, with report as required under section 4, for his decision regarding acquisition. The Divisional Commissioner turned down the objection containing illogical demands of the writ petitioner-respondents and 'approved the acquisition. The PGCL further claimed that other than the writ petitioner-respondents no other person raised any objection in acquiring the said land for the said purpose which is very much for public purpose and in public interest. After finalization of the matter by the Divisional Commissioner under section 5, notices under section 6 were issued and served upon all the owners including the writ petitioner-respondents on 8-10-2007 asking the affected owners to appear in the office of the Deputy Commissioner on 25-10-2007 and to submit their verbal as well as written statements as to the nature, quantum and demand in support of the property. The notices of the writ petitioner respondent No. 1 was duly served at her given address at "Dhanshiri Apartment" 35, Indira Road, Dhaka, but the process server having found her absent at the said address the notices were served upon the "Darwan" of the said apartment. Thus the allegation of non service of any notice upon the writ petitioner-respondents is totally false. 

 5. The writ respondent No. 8 further claimed that the acquisition has been completed and the Deputy Commissioner has determined the compensation under section 7 of the Ordinance 1982, and total amount of compensation has been deposited by the requiring body and payment has been made to the interested persons who appeared before the Deputy Commissioner. It is further contended that the allegation of the writ petitioner-respondents that their 2.02 acres of land has been acquired is not correct. Actually 1.43 acres of land from Plots No. 49 and 51 under South-Duttapara Mouza and Plot No. 69 under South Dattapara Mouza has been acquired wherein the writ petitioners are not the absolute owners rather they are co-sharers with many other persons who have not been made parties in the writ petition and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable. It is further contended that after the acquisition process having been complete and possession has been taken over, and 90% earth filling works of the project has been completed and it being one of the National Development projects for public purpose and in public interest, the work is being done rapidly. As to the allegation of non-specification of the acquired land it has been stated that the lands of plot Nos. 69, 51 and 49 sought to be acquired has been well specified by preparing a map delineating the portions of those plots sought to be acquired and well specified by demarcating the area of the lands acquired. Thus the said allegation is not true and/or not tenable in law. Accordingly the Rule Nisi should be discharged. 

 6. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record held that an agreement between the requiring body and the Government has been signed and executed before the acquisition as per requirement of section 15 of the Ordinance and the acquisition in question was for public interest and for public purpose, but opined that the lands acquired having not been specified and demarcated the acquisition was not legal. Consequently, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and declared the acquisition in question to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect, by the impugned judgment and order dated 7-12-2009. 

 8. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellant mainly submits that the High Court Division has committed wrong in holding that the land acquired has not been duly specified without fully considering the map wherein the portions of the acquired land in the plots have been specifically delineated. The said map was produced before the High Court Division and it perused the same but did not consider it to its true perspective while passing the impugned judgment. The learned Advocate further submits that where a map showing the demarcation of the acquired land, was produced before the High Court Division, it should have taken the same into consideration or could have directed the authority to produce any other or further material, if necessary, or a more distinct copy of the same before discarding the same altogether and declaring that the land acquired was not specified. He submits that the central land allotment committee approved the acquisition of these lands on the basis of this map on 23-5-2007 and the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 was issued on 27-6-2007 and in the circumstances it cannot be said that the land sought to be acquired is vague and unspecified. Mr Alam further submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that portion of land from a big plot can be acquired upon delineating the same by preparing a map which is the only way to identify and specify the land proposed to be acquired. In this respect, he submits that in the project proposal dated 1-11-2006 it has been stated that 'the site layout plan was prepared and attached with the record for acquiring 6.00 acres of land from the aforesaid two mouzas'. In the Plot Index of LA Case No. 13/2006-2007, it has been mentioned that 'along with other plots, 0.77 acre of land out of 1.11 acre from the northern side of Plot No. 49, 0.40 acre of land out of 1.21 acre from the northern side of Plot No. 51 and 0.26 acre of land out of 0.86 from the northern side of Plot No. 69 has been demarcated for acquisition and, as such the allegation that the plots have not been specified, demarcated and delineated is not at all correct. Referring to the report under section 4(2) of the Ordinance Mr Alam submits that the respondents herein and others filed objection under section 4(1) of the said Ordinance on 12-7-2007 upon receiving notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance dated 1-7-2007. Objection was raised only to exclude 0.26 + 0.40 = 0.66 acre of land from their plots situated in South Duttapara and South Ramchandrapur mouzas from acquisition on the ground that 'in case the said quantum of land is acquired then there will remain no other place for their homestead which will cause irreparable loss to them'. Referring to the aforesaid position Mr Alam submits that the objection as to non demarcation or non specification or even non delineation of the land proposed to be acquired has not been raised before the authority concerned. According to him, if no such objection as to non demarcation or non specification or even non delineation of the land proposed to be acquired has not been raised before the authority concerned in the objection pursuant to notice under section 3, such objection cannot be raised anywhere subsequently and, as such, non demarcation or non specification or even non delineation of the land proposed to be acquired cannot be a ground for cancelling the acquisition. In this respect he referred to the case of Mizanur Rahman vs DC Mymensingh, (7 BLC (AD) 171. The learned advocate, lastly, submits that in this case the land was acquired for one of the most important public purpose and in public interest by following all the requirements of law and there has been no illegality in the process of acquisition and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division declaring the acquisition illegal has kept the whole project stayed causing inconveniences and suffering to all, specially, the newly set up tannery industry. Thus the impugned judgment and order needs to be interfered with this Division. 

 10. It appears from the materials on record that the government took decision to acquire 5.79 acres of land from different plots of the aforesaid two mouzas for the purpose of establishing high voltage "Power Greed Sub-Station" to meet the urgent need of power supply for the tannery industries and other industrial units which is for public purpose and in public interest. Thereafter upon completion of feasibility tests and all legal formalities the said quantum of land has been acquired and handed over to the requiring body PGCL (the appellant) who has completed earth filling upto 90%. The main contention of Mr Alam is that the High Court Division rightly held that the property has been acquired for public purpose and in public interest and upon executing an agreement with the requiring body as per section 15 of the Ordinance of 1982 but declared the acquisition in question to be without lawful authority holding that the land has not been specified and demarcated. According to him the High Court Division failed to consider the sketch-map in its true perspective, which specifically specified and demarcated the land proposed to be acquired in the plots. 

 11. From the record it appears that the writ petitioners filed the writ petition challenging the LA Case along with the notices under section 6 of the said Ordinance 1982 on the ground firstly that there was no agreement signed between the requiring body and the acquiring body i.e. the Government; 2nd July the acquisition was not for public purpose and in public interest; thirdly there was no specification, delineation of the portion of different plots; fourthly no notice under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance has been served upon her. 

 12. The High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment found the first two grounds i.e. signing of the agreement between the requiring body and the acquiring body to have been done as per requirement of section 15 of the Ordinance 1982 and also found that the acquisition of the land sought to be acquired is for public purpose and in public interest. But made the Rule Nisi absolute on the ground of non-specification and non-delineation of the portion of different plots. Since the High Court Division found the agreement to have been signed as per requirement of section 15 and the acquisition was for public purpose and public interest we do not need to address the said two issues. 

 14. From the pleadings of the parties it appears that the writ petitioners filed objection on 6-8-2007 and thereby requested the Deputy Commissioner not to acquire her property not on the ground of non-specification or non-delineation but on the ground that 'if the same is acquired then there will remain no other place for their homestead'. It further appears that the process-server went to the address of writ petitioner No. 1 at Dhanshiri Apartment, 35, Indira Road, Dhaka but having found her absent the notices were served upon the Darwan of the Apartment. Apart from the aforesaid position it appears that the writ respondent in its affidavit-in-opposition categorically stated that "a public notice of the same has also been duly served on the conspicuous place of the properties proposed to be acquired and upon the interested persons and others". Hence it appears that the writ petitioner cannot under such circumstances say that the notices were not served upon her. Moreover, it is not the requirement of law that notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance No. II of 1982 have to be served upon a person having interest in the land or on the owner of the land when the property is acquired for public purpose and in public interest as apparent from the language employed in sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance 1982. 

 16. Thus only question remains is whether the land proposed to be acquired has been specified and/or delineated by the acquiring body. It is on record that the writ petitioners filed objection on 6-8-2007, after the notice under section 3 was served, requesting the Deputy Commissioner not to acquire their property on compassionate ground but not on the ground of non specification of the property proposed to be acquired. Such plea was never raised by the writ petitioners in the said objection or before any authority. On the other hand, in the affidavit-in-opposition of writ respondent No. 8 (the present appellant), it has been specifically claimed that a layout plan and sketch-map of the land proposed to be acquired were prepared on conducting a field survey by the authority which was affixed with the project profile and filed before the High Court Division. But the said statement in the affidavit-in-opposition of the writ respondent No. 8 remained uncontroverted. Moreover, it is not the requirement of law that a notice under section 3 or 6 has to be accompanied by acquisition map showing specification of the land in case of acquisition of part of a big plot. In the instant case, it appears that such specification has been made by preparing a map delineating the portions of the land of Plots No. 69, 51 and 49 on record and the writ petitioners never raised the question of non-specification of land in their objection anywhere under section 4 of the Ordinance as mentioned above. 'When a proceeding is initiated for acquisition of some lands acquired for public purpose and in public interest and when notices under sections 3 and 6 were served and no objection as to specification or indefiniteness of the property was raised before the acquisition authority after the notices under the aforesaid provisions of law were served, such objection cannot be raised before any' authority, subsequently, including the High Court Division' as has been decided in the case of Mizanur Rahman vs DC Mymensingh [7 BLC (AD) 171.
